added_provisions.reason: Notaries Ordinance s.31, proviso to rule (17): the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the registry search. An exception to the central duty of the answer was missing from the map.

Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3A(3): requirements for a power of attorney executed outside Sri Lanka. It is the cross-reference that makes s.3B(1) apply, and the enrichment places the power of attorney in Melbourne, so it is indispensable to the attorney limb.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (15A)(c): the attorney must give the notary an affidavit that the power is genuine and in force and the grantor alive. A required document on the attorney limb that the map omitted.

Registration of Documents Ordinance s.13(5): the Registrar shall refuse to register an instrument lacking the required particulars. Supplies the refusal limb asserted in CL-M002-Q01-007, which the cited s.13(1) does not contain.

Registration of Documents Ordinance s.32(5): the court may order a later instrument rectified or cancelled. Supplies the remedy limb asserted in CL-M002-Q01-005, which the cited s.32(1) does not contain.
Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3C: a power of attorney is valid for only five years from execution unless it states its own period. A check on the attorney limb the map omitted.

Two indispensable provisions and four supporting provisions were added. One conclusion claim (CL-M002-Q01-023) is marked disputed; every other claim is verified.

disagreements.researcher_position: CL-M002-Q01-023: the notary should satisfy himself from the root of title and the registry entries that no State grant condition or acquisition affects the land, resting on Prescription Ordinance s.3, Land Acquisition Act s.2(1) and Land Development Ordinance s.46(1).
disagreements.verifier_position: The possession limb is supported, but Land Acquisition Act s.2(1) describes a notice exhibited in the area for a preliminary investigation, not anything a notary would find in a registry folio, and Land Development Ordinance s.46(1) states the prohibition while the nullity is in s.46(3). The 'registry entries' route to an acquisition check is not supported by either cited provision.

disagreements.researcher_position: Registration of Documents Ordinance sections 13 and 32 are unamended or amended only in ways that do not affect the excerpts relied on.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus edition of that Ordinance is the 1990 consolidation, while the corpus separately holds Acts No. 48 of 2011 (substitutes s.13(1)), No. 21 of 2013 (amends s.13(6)), No. 32 of 2022 (substitutes s.32(1), extends the caveator's period to sixty days) and No. 18 of 2024 (repeals Chapter IV). The section text relied on is therefore not the text in force at April 2026, even though the substance relied on survives.

disagreements.researcher_position: M002-Q01 is statute_only; conveyancing conventions such as tracing thirty years of title are refinements of the statutory search duty.
disagreements.verifier_position: Retained as statute_only, because the Notaries Ordinance, the Registration of Documents Ordinance, the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act and the Powers of Attorney Ordinance between them yield a complete document list. Flagged for the lawyer because the depth of the title search, and the practice of tracing thirty years, comes from conveyancing practice rather than any provision in the corpus.

unsupported_claims: CL-M002-Q01-023 (conclusion): the acquisition and State-grant limb is inferential and neither Land Acquisition Act s.2(1) nor Land Development Ordinance s.46(1) supports finding it through registry entries. Marked disputed, not deleted.
CL-M002-Q01-007 as filed asserted refusal of registration on s.13(1) alone; refusal is in s.13(5). Repaired by adding PROV-M002-904 to the claim's supporting provisions.
CL-M002-Q01-005 as filed asserted rectification or cancellation on s.32(1) alone; that remedy is in s.32(5). Repaired by adding PROV-M002-905.
temporal_issues: 23-1927/s12 chain: the Registration of Documents Ordinance sections are served from the 1990 consolidation while four later amending Acts sit in the same corpus (48-2011, 21-2013, 32-2022, 18-2024). Recorded as a new corpus_gaps entry.
38-2014/s2: the researcher's temporal note credits Acts No. 3 of 2017 and No. 21 of 2018 with amending section 2; in the corpus those Acts insert and amend sections 5A and 3.

The seven Notaries Ordinance s.31 provisions rest on a consolidated body in which rules (16), (17) and the thumb-impression rule are printed without their numbers, so their subsection labels are not machine-checkable. The researcher flagged this; it is confirmed and recorded on each provision.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Proviso to Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17) dispensing with the search on written authority of the parties - added as PROV-M002-901.
Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3A(3) (requirements for a power executed abroad) and s.3C (five-year validity) - added as PROV-M002-902 and PROV-M002-906.
Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (15A)(c), the attorney's affidavit that the power is genuine, in force and the grantor alive - added as PROV-M002-903.

Not added, but noted for the lawyer: Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3(1)(b) requires a power executed outside Sri Lanka to be submitted for registration within three months of execution, which on the enriched facts is a live check; Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2(2) requires the foreign shareholding to stay below fifty per cent for twenty years and voids the transfer if it does not, s.4(4) imposes six-monthly reporting by the company secretary, and s.3(1)(i) exempts listed companies; s.25 defines 'foreigner' and 'foreign company'. None of these appear in the map.

Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (17)(b)(iii) requires passport photographs of the signatories and copies of their identity documents attached to the protocol for a deed of transfer - a document requirement the checklist does not mention.
case_law_dependence: No case law is cited anywhere in the map. The only practice-based element is the depth of the title search, recorded above as an authority_requirement disagreement.
enrichment_issues: M002-Q01: the enriched background names several of the very documents the answer lists (certificate of incorporation and its number, board resolution authorising the managing director, survey plan, power of attorney, the single 2011 deed). The facts are needed to make the scenario determinate, but they lower the difficulty of a question whose task is to name those documents.

M002-Q01, FACT-M002-Q01-006: 'has fenced off and cultivated ... since 2009 and pays nothing' tracks the statutory test in Prescription Ordinance s.3 ('possession unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce') closely enough to hand the candidate the legal characterisation.
No statute name or section number is leaked in the enriched background, and no conclusion is stated. Every synthetic_decisive fact carries a reason and a counterfactual effect.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: M002-Q04 (Tier B: where, how and within how many days the stamp duty is paid) is absent from the legal map, correctly, since the map covers Tier A only. Worth noting that the corpus does hold material on it (Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act ss.8 and 9, Stamp Duty Act s.45, Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (7)(a)-(c)), so Q04 may not be blocked in the way Q03 is.
